content: Minoxidil, when taken orally, may increase the risk of chest pain (angina) or other heart-related issues. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor to monitor for any symptoms or changes in your condition. If you experience chest pain or notice it worsening while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Your doctor may prescribe additional medications as part of your minoxidil treatment plan. Do not discontinue any prescribed medications unless explicitly instructed by your doctor. Minoxidil is prescribed in combination with other drugs to manage high blood pressure. It works by relaxing blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily throughout the body. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Minoxidil is available in tablet form and is typically taken once or twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take minoxidil exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. While minoxidil helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before starting minoxidil, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to minoxidil or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other blood pressure medications, diuretics (water pills), guanethidine, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had heart disease, a heart attack, pheochromocytoma, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking minoxidil, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform the doctor or dentist that you are taking minoxidil. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can exacerbate the side effects of minoxidil. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of minoxidil, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Minoxidil may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: increased size or darkening of fine body hair, dizziness, breast tenderness, rash, headache, upset stomach, or vomiting. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, or those mentioned in the important warning section, contact your doctor immediately: rapid heartbeat, swollen ankles or feet, unexplained weight gain, difficulty breathing, or fainting. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store minoxidil in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Regular blood pressure checks are necessary to monitor your response to minoxidil. Your doctor may also order tests such as an electrocardiogram (EKG) to assess heart function. You may be asked to check your pulse (heart rate) daily; ask your doctor or pharmacist for instructions. Notify your doctor if your resting heart rate increases by more than 20 beats per minute. Weigh yourself daily and report any rapid weight gain to your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
